publicReleaseNotes:
Orbit 0.4.9 adds saved record views, separately authorized Gmail sending and reviewed imports from a connected Pipedrive account. Orbit still runs on rer 0.2.107.

- **Save the record lists you use.** Save a contact, company or deal list with its search, filters, visible columns and sort order. Keep it private or make it available to the workspace, update or delete it, and reopen it against current records and permissions. Saved views retain definitions, not a frozen copy of the results. Archived custom fields remain readable in saved views, and deal amounts use the workspace currency.
- **Choose an authorized Gmail mailbox when reviewing a message.** Reconnect a Google capture source with separate mailbox-send consent, then select that mailbox in the draft's send review. Approval binds the saved recipient, rendered content and sending mailbox; a changed review needs fresh approval. Sent history identifies the mailbox. A paused, disconnected or refused mailbox does not switch to another sender. Uncertain delivery is reconciled against Sent without automatically submitting the same approval again. Microsoft mailbox sending remains unavailable because its connection does not request the permission needed to create a draft. Read access and calendar writeback stay separate from send consent.
- **Review a connected Pipedrive import before applying it.** The installation owner can supply a read-only OAuth token and pull organizations, people, USD deals, pipeline and stage metadata, supported scalar custom fields and linked notes into the existing saved dry-run and Apply flow. Pulls keep checkpoints across interruptions and rate limits. Map source stages and contact or company owners before previewing; deal owners remain source history. New contacts start as Do not contact, missing source marketing status also holds an existing match, and existing stops win. This pull requires a USD workspace, never converts amounts, and is limited to 1,000 rows per entity and 2 MB of source review data. Leads, products, activities, files and automations need separate reconciliation; unsupported fields retain source references and export guidance. Orbit writes nothing back to Pipedrive. Credentials, checkpoints and connected review authority stay out of archives; reconnect and pull again after a restore.
- **Draft and activity wording follows what happened.** A reply that makes a handwritten draft stale asks for review without claiming a scheduled follow-up was cancelled. Contact permission uses ordinary wording in that review. Record activity names task creation, completion, cancellation, reassignment, rescheduling and recurring occurrences.
- **Record and workflow pages recover more consistently.** A missing record offers the same recovery when related reads finish in a different order. Previewing an active workflow's draft keeps one editor. Older native archives remain recognized, with new mailbox-history fields initialized from their migration defaults and restored mailbox send authority withheld until fresh consent.

Account proposals remain limited to selected written evidence and the existing three proposal types. Scheduled graph maintenance, transcripts, licensed enrichment and broader stakeholder inference remain incomplete. Workflow undo remains partial. The earlier erasure limitations remain: a former sponsor or approver can still appear by name in a colleague's timeline and audit rows, and an approver's name stays in the search index until it is rebuilt. These changes do not establish complete agent coverage, complete migration from another CRM or live-provider acceptance.

Update from 0.4.8 in place after stopping writes and taking a private backup. Apply the three pending migrations once, in order, before the new Worker serves: 0088 adds saved record views, 0089 adds installation-local mailbox send consent and message provenance, and 0090 adds private Pipedrive connection and pull staging. Existing mailbox connections gain no send authority. Preserve the migration ledger and every already-applied migration; installations using intermediate migration names need their ledger and schema reconciled first. No new provider setting is required to retain existing features. Optional Gmail sending needs fresh explicit send consent and message review; optional Pipedrive pulls need the owner's read-only OAuth access. Older installations must first account for earlier pending migrations and release instructions.

migrations.buyerSteps: Apply once after 0087 and before the new Worker serves. Adds versioned saved record view definitions; opening a saved view rechecks current record authority. Preserve all previously applied migrations and their ledger entries.

Apply once after 0088 and before the new Worker serves. Adds installation-local mailbox send authorizations and message provenance columns. Existing mailbox connections gain no send authority; sending requires fresh explicit consent and review. Preserve all previously applied migrations and their ledger entries.

Apply once after 0089 and before the new Worker serves. Adds installation-local Pipedrive credentials, source pull checkpoints and saved connected-review authority. No records are imported automatically. Optional pulls require the installation owner to connect read-only OAuth access; credentials and staging are excluded from archives and require a new connection and pull after restore. Preserve all previously applied migrations and their ledger entries.

agentUpdateInstructions: Update from 0.4.8 in place; never reset or replace the installation. Stop local dev and hosted writes and take a private backup outside the checkout, using rer export locally or Records → Export archive when hosted. Check out v0.4.9 and run rer install with pinned Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and rer 0.2.107. Use rer setup locally or rer deploy --env-file .dev.vars.deploy when hosted. Preserve the migration ledger: apply only pending migrations 0088_saved_record_views.sql, 0089_mailbox_send.sql and 0090_pipedrive_import.sql, once in order and before the new Worker serves or writes resume. Keep every already-applied migration and owner customization; 0085_meeting_follow_up.sql, 0086_hubspot_import.sql and 0087_hubspot_explicit_erasure.sql belong to 0.4.8 and must not be replayed. Installations that applied an intermediate candidate under earlier migration names need their ledger and schema reconciled before treating this as a routine upgrade; no automatic remapping is claimed. Older installations must first account for their earlier pending migrations and release-history instructions. Existing mailbox connections gain no send authority. Optional Gmail sending requires reconnection with separate explicit send consent and exact-content review; Microsoft mailbox sending remains unavailable. Optional Pipedrive imports require the installation owner’s read-only OAuth token, a USD workspace and a new saved dry run before Apply. Pipedrive credentials, checkpoints and connected review authority do not travel in archives; reconnect and pull again after restore. Restored mailbox history retains provenance without restoring send authority. No new provider setting is required to retain existing features. Keep the prior Mailchimp webhook checks and owner confirmation for held deletion requests after reconnection or restore. Before resuming writes, check existing records, saved views, capture evidence and proposals, follow-up history and paused reminders, drafts, scheduled messages, mailbox history, forms, reports, notifications and integration settings. Retain the release-note limitations on graph maintenance, agent coverage, workflow undo, erasure and supported import scope.
